claims.text: Brittle behavior in initially single-phase high-entropy alloys emerges because nanoscale ordered domains or short-range order form within the matrix.
Nanoscale ordered domains or short-range order act as stress concentrators.
Nanoscale ordered domains or short-range order inhibit dislocation motion under certain thermal and mechanical loading conditions.
The initial alloy is single-phase and has a homogeneous microstructure with no detectable secondary phases or significant segregation.
Intermediate-temperature thermal aging promotes nanoscale ordered domains or short-range order while secondary-phase formation can be avoided.
Nanoscale ordered domains or short-range order increase local lattice resistance to dislocation motion.
Increased local lattice resistance produces stress concentration and crack initiation under applied mechanical loads.
Stress concentration and crack initiation caused by ordered domains or short-range order reduce toughness.
Thermally aged HEAs will have lower fracture toughness than the as-cast or solution-treated baseline.
Thermally aged HEAs will exhibit greater brittleness than the baseline.
The predicted toughness loss and brittleness will be particularly pronounced at cryogenic temperatures.
The as-cast or solution-treated baseline contains no nanoscale ordered domains or short-range order.
The hypothesis applies to HEAs subjected to intermediate-temperature aging.
The hypothesis does not apply when aging temperatures are too low to induce short-range order.
The hypothesis does not apply when aging temperatures are high enough to cause significant grain coarsening or secondary-phase formation.
The relationship among aging conditions, short-range-order development, and mechanical properties may vary with alloy composition.
